question.problem:
Use the model below to calculate $\dfrac{1}{4} \div 4.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14129811/assets/8eccf163bffabb43593188590a1f995544f3d1ac0aebcdd87dce638b230f8165.png)
question.worked_solution:
Since we need to divide by $\color{blue}4$, we split the whole into $\color{blue}4$ equal parts horizontally.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14129811/assets/a34a3fb198ef2ea79f8baf8f0acbdbdc179c6259c614824315d3d96e5ea4e921.png)

From the picture on the right, we obtain that the shaded part represents $\dfrac{1}{16}$ of the whole.

Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{1}{4} \div 4 = \dfrac{1}{16}\,.
$$
